reasons: The redline replaces Singapore law with New York law, landing squarely on the playbook preferred position (accepted governing law set), so it is directionally correct.

Deleting the Singapore exclusive-jurisdiction grant is justified and safe: Section 28.2 already confers exclusive jurisdiction on the state and federal courts in New York County, so the customer retains an accepted forum and the internal conflict is resolved.

The high changed-character ratio is explained by the rule requiring substitution of the jurisdiction words and removal of the conflicting foreign venue grant; the sentence structure ('This Agreement is governed exclusively by...') is preserved.

The comment is accurate, correctly cites the New York preferred position, notes the reason for deleting the Singapore venue, and offers the Delaware/California/England and Wales fallback in the prescribed tone.

Minor note for the drafter: the added 'without regard to its conflict of laws principles' phrase goes slightly beyond the minimal edit; it is standard and not prejudicial to us, but could be dropped if the counterparty resists any language not required by the rule.
